section_summary.extract_value: This section presents a theoretical discussion of the object-as-process dichotomy in body image research, reviewing literature on how women tend to focus on body appearance (object) while men focus on body function (process). The text synthesizes empirical evidence showing that viewing the body-as-process is associated with more positive body image outcomes, particularly for women, and proposes that conversations about diet and exercise may differentially impact body image through this theoretical framework. No original empirical study data is presented in this section.
